mission_2.prediction: I predict that A* will finish sooner than BFS on the constrained map. In Mission 1, both algorithms found shortest paths, but A* generally explored fewer cells because it uses the Manhattan distance heuristic to guide its search. BFS explores cells in order using a queue without considering their distance to the goal. I think A* will plan faster, although the actual navigation time may depend on the turns and obstacles along the route.
mission_2.performance: I predicted that A* would finish sooner than BFS because it uses a heuristic to find a path more efficiently. On the constrained map, both planners succeeded. BFS took 89.17 seconds and traveled 23.90 meters, while A* took 89.68 seconds and traveled 23.90 meters. My prediction was not supported because BFS finished slightly faster. Both planners followed nearly identical routes, but small differences in tracking and turns can affect execution time. The plots show that even when two planners find equally short paths, the robot may not finish at exactly the same time.
mission_2.choice: I would choose Nav2 as my delivery planner because it successfully reached the goal on both maps and performed consistently. On the open map, Nav2 finished in 35.50 seconds, and on the constrained map, it finished in 73.36 seconds. Compared with BFS, which took 46.40 and 89.17 seconds, Nav2 was faster on both maps and traveled shorter distances. Nav2 traveled 10.10 meters on the open map and 20.56 meters on the constrained map, while BFS traveled 13.17 and 23.90 meters. For a delivery robot, I think reliably reaching the destination while minimizing travel time and distance is more important than simply finding a path quickly.
